focus: Shared helpers, process-spawn density and the doctor suite: which infrastructure costs more than it returns
noveltyJustification: 6 of 7 findings were fully new (load-bearing setup, repo-wide census, spawn density, doctor density, doctor language split, double wiring) and 1 partially new (no helper sprawl).
keyQuestions: Which test infrastructure (custom harnesses, serial lists, shared fixtures, helper layers) costs run time or maintenance without proportional coverage?
answeredQuestions: Which test infrastructure (custom harnesses, serial lists, shared fixtures, helper layers) costs run time or maintenance without proportional coverage?

Calling the doctor folder three parallel frameworks
Treating spawn-heavy tests as overengineering by default

graphEvents.label: Which test infrastructure costs more than it returns
Process spawn density is the per-test cost driver

label: The shared vitest setup is load-bearing: 71 lines forcing absolute TMPDIR and production-DB isolation, loaded by three configs
Repository tracks 1173 test files outside specs and vendored trees: 702 vitest.ts, 209 test.cjs, 97 test.mjs, 66 py, 64 test.ts, 35 sh
Process spawning dominates per-test cost: 464 spawn sites in 121 spec-kit files, 128 in 43 deep-loop files, 85 in 32 advisor files, 176 in 36 doctor files
Doctor suite has the highest spawn density (36 of 59 files, 176 sites) behind one bash aggregator with a three-tool dependency contract
Doctor folder is 54 node:test cjs suites plus 4 bash and 1 python, not three co-equal frameworks
Doctor tree is wired twice: spec-kit-check runs the aggregator and opencode-dual-version runs opencode-version-battery explicitly
No duplicated helper layer exists: deep-loop keeps one 71-line hermetic path helper while advisor loads the spec-kit setup
